llm.summary: This is a coherent local text-to-speech skill, but its optional playback feature can execute unintended shell commands through the output filename.

dimensions.detail: Local file output and a one-time remote model dependency are proportionate for TTS and disclosed, though the model reference is not pinned to an immutable revision.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer or persistence setup is present; setup requires Python packages plus espeak-ng, and the metadata discloses outbound network for a first-run Hugging Face model download.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents Python usage, voice profiles, WAV output, and first-run model download, but it does not clearly warn that playback invokes a shell command and the output path is not constrained or safely handled.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, credential access, or privilege escalation code was found, but the playback command injection would run arbitrary commands with the invoking user's privileges if an unsafe output path is used with --play.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main purpose, generating WAV audio with Kokoro voices, matches the files shipped, but artifact/scripts/speak.py also offers --play and passes the output path into os.system, creating command-execution risk beyond simple TTS generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing or using. The TTS purpose is legitimate and most behavior is disclosed, but avoid --play and do not pass untrusted output paths unless the playback code is fixed to use a non-shell subprocess call or equivalent safe audio playback. Also consider whether a first-run Hugging Face model download without a pinned revision fits your environment's supply-chain requirements.
llm.findings:
[AST5] unexpected: Accepted. artifact/scripts/speak.py returns the user-controlled --output path and interpolates it into os.system when --play is used, which is a real command-injection flaw.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted. The static finding is supported by the same artifact evidence: os.system receives an unquoted output path derived from user arguments.
[LP3] expected: Partly downgraded. Python execution and file output are expected for this skill, and network use is disclosed in metadata, but tighter declared tool scope would improve governance.
[SDI-1] expected: Partly downgraded. Hugging Face download/use is disclosed in SKILL.md and metadata as the Kokoro model source; the remaining issue is supply-chain hygiene because no revision or hash is pinned.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in context. Playing generated audio is related to TTS, but implementing it through a shell call is unnecessary and materially increases local execution risk.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in context. The --play flag signals playback, but the user-facing instructions do not disclose that enabling it launches a shell command.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded. The predefined voice profiles and locale-coded voices are visible and configurable through --voice or --agent; this is not a security concern by itself.
